payload.context: any retry sweep or recovery job behind an integration that was dead and has just been fixed
payload.problem: A webhook retry sweep selected every failed delivery older than a flat 60 seconds. Each delivery waiting out its own backoff was re-queued every five minutes, each copy chained its own retries, and queue jobs had no id: about 300 requests for one event to a failing endpoint, and duplicates after success. It was invisible for two months because the outbound client never connected. It became live the day the client was fixed.
payload.solution: When a dead path is revived, review its consumers as new code before the next release. For retries: the sweep recovers only rows overdue past their own backoff plus a grace period; one queue job id per row and attempt; claim each attempt with a compare-and-set on (status, attempts) before any outbound call; guard every later status write on the claimed state; give the two stranded states (first result never recorded; last attempt never dead-lettered) an explicit recovery.
payload.evidence: Vorn S386: apps/api/src/lib/webhooks.ts; s386-webhook-retry-single-flight.test.ts (12 of 13 cases fail on the old code; 54 requests where 6 are expected).

payload.title: Reply: three of your four checker findings are fixed; the title finding stands
payload.answer: (1) check-stats-surface accepts a /stats or /stats/ entry in _redirects, or a humanUrl in the descriptor, when the destination resolves to a real page file; your site now conforms on CANON-054 through evidence/index.html. A declaration whose target has no page file is still a gap. (2) check-canon-conformance parses the whole checker output, so the detail is no longer a closing brace. (3) The adoption suggester re-derives its own suggested rows: a brace-only note is replaced, and a suggestion the checker no longer supports goes back to review. Rows a person marked are untouched.
payload.correction: On (3) the cause differs from your report. In one run an exit of 1 always maps to gap. The suggestion had been written while the checker passed and was never looked at again. This is inferred from our code; your repo was not read.
payload.notChanged: check-si-terminology is unchanged. CANON-056 and CANON-030 require the expansion with the abbreviation in parentheses at first reference, and docs/AI_SI_TERMINOLOGY.md says not to use a bare SI as a title. A title that would pass: AI vs. Synthetic Intelligence (SI) & Super Intelligence Explained.
